## 1. Load files

```{r, load_files, echo=FALSE}
# item29: 5 duplicate runs per scenario (item29_tair10_sd_raw.sh)
reps <- 1:5

load_scenario_reps <- function(n){
  lapply(reps, function(i){
    SIM <- file.path(WRK, sprintf('output/TEgenomeSimulator_tair10_sd_scenario%s_rep%d_result', n, i))
    prefix <- sprintf('tair10_sd_scenario%s_rep%d', n, i)
    list(
      genomefai = read.table(file.path(SIM, paste0(prefix, '_genome_sequence_out_final.fasta.fai')), header = FALSE, sep = '\t'),
      tefai = read.table(file.path(SIM, paste0(prefix, '_repeat_sequence_out_final.fasta.fai')), header = FALSE, sep = '\t', comment.char = ""),
      tegff = read.table(file.path(SIM, paste0(prefix, '_repeat_annotation_out_final.gff')), header = FALSE, sep = '\t', comment.char = "")
    )
  })
}

scenario1_list <- load_scenario_reps('1')
scenario2_list <- load_scenario_reps('2')
scenario3_list <- load_scenario_reps('3')
scenario4_list <- load_scenario_reps('4')

# rep 1 aliased to the original single-genome variable names, used unchanged by the
# existing (single-representative-genome) histogram section below
tegff1 <- scenario1_list[[1]]$tegff
tegff2 <- scenario2_list[[1]]$tegff
tegff3 <- scenario3_list[[1]]$tegff
tegff4 <- scenario4_list[[1]]$tegff

genomesize1 <- sum(scenario1_list[[1]]$genomefai$V2); tesize1 <- sum(scenario1_list[[1]]$tefai$V2); te_perc1 <- tesize1 * 100 / genomesize1
genomesize2 <- sum(scenario2_list[[1]]$genomefai$V2); tesize2 <- sum(scenario2_list[[1]]$tefai$V2); te_perc2 <- tesize2 * 100 / genomesize2
genomesize3 <- sum(scenario3_list[[1]]$genomefai$V2); tesize3 <- sum(scenario3_list[[1]]$tefai$V2); te_perc3 <- tesize3 * 100 / genomesize3
genomesize4 <- sum(scenario4_list[[1]]$genomefai$V2); tesize4 <- sum(scenario4_list[[1]]$tefai$V2); te_perc4 <- tesize4 * 100 / genomesize4

data.sum1 <- te_by_superfamily_sim_genome(tegff1); total_loci1 <- sum(data.sum1$count)
data.sum2 <- te_by_superfamily_sim_genome(tegff2); total_loci2 <- sum(data.sum2$count)
data.sum3 <- te_by_superfamily_sim_genome(tegff3); total_loci3 <- sum(data.sum3$count)
data.sum4 <- te_by_superfamily_sim_genome(tegff4); total_loci4 <- sum(data.sum4$count)

breakdown1 <- te_breakdown_sim_genome(tegff1)
breakdown2 <- te_breakdown_sim_genome(tegff2)
breakdown3 <- te_breakdown_sim_genome(tegff3)
breakdown4 <- te_breakdown_sim_genome(tegff4)

# all 5 replicates, tagged with rep - used for the mean +/- SD line graph further down
breakdown1_allreps <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(reps, function(i){ bd <- te_breakdown_sim_genome(scenario1_list[[i]]$tegff); bd$rep <- i; bd }))
breakdown2_allreps <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(reps, function(i){ bd <- te_breakdown_sim_genome(scenario2_list[[i]]$tegff); bd$rep <- i; bd }))
breakdown3_allreps <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(reps, function(i){ bd <- te_breakdown_sim_genome(scenario3_list[[i]]$tegff); bd$rep <- i; bd }))
breakdown4_allreps <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(reps, function(i){ bd <- te_breakdown_sim_genome(scenario4_list[[i]]$tegff); bd$rep <- i; bd }))
```

of the same data would show.

## 3. Test RepeatMasker recovery rate (5 replicates per scenario)

Heatmap cells show the mean of the replicate recovery rates; a replicate with no simulated TE
in a cell is skipped, and cells empty in all 5 replicates are grey. Numbers in the cells are the
mean number of simulated TEs per replicate (k = thousands). Marginal bars show the
pooled rate of each slice, sum(recovered) / sum(total), computed within each replicate and then
summarised as mean ± SD across the 5 replicates.

```{r, load_files_recovery, echo=FALSE}
load_recovery_reps <- function(n){
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(reps, function(i){
    SIM <- file.path(WRK, sprintf('output/TEgenomeSimulator_tair10_sd_scenario%s_rep%d_result', n, i))
    read.table(file.path(SIM, 'RM_recovery_eval/recovery_by_bin2D.tsv'), header = TRUE, sep = "\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
      mutate(scenario = paste0('scenario', n), rep = i)
  }))
}

scenarios <- c('scenario1', 'scenario2', 'scenario3', 'scenario4')

bindf <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(1:4, load_recovery_reps)) |>
  mutate(rate = ifelse(total == 0, NA, rate))
```

```{r, prep_heatmap, echo=FALSE}
# main heatmap data: mean of replicate rates per cell; sd, cv and n_reps (replicates with >= 1 TE
# in the cell) are kept for the supplementary variability figure only
heat_data <- bindf %>%
  group_by(scenario, integrity_interval, identity_interval) %>%
  summarise(n_reps = sum(total > 0),
            n_mean = mean(total),
            sd_rate = if (n_reps > 1) sd(rate, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
            rate = if (n_reps > 0) mean(rate, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
            .groups="drop") %>%
  mutate(cv_rate = ifelse(rate > 0, sd_rate / rate, NA_real_))

# pooled rate of a slice within each replicate, then mean +/- SD across replicates
pooled_marginal <- function(df, slice_col){
  df %>%
    group_by(scenario, rep, .data[[slice_col]]) %>%
    summarise(rate = ifelse(sum(total) == 0, NA_real_, sum(recovered) / sum(total)), .groups="drop") %>%
    group_by(scenario, .data[[slice_col]]) %>%
    summarise(sd = sd(rate, na.rm = TRUE), rate = mean(rate, na.rm = TRUE), .groups="drop") %>%
    filter(!is.nan(rate)) %>%
    mutate(ymin = pmax(rate - sd, 0), ymax = pmin(rate + sd, 1))
}

# top marginal rate by integrity_interval
marg_x <- pooled_marginal(bindf, "integrity_interval")

# right marginal rate by identity_interval
marg_y <- pooled_marginal(bindf, "identity_interval")

# all bin labels, so marginal bar axes match the heatmap even when a slice is empty
integrity_bins <- sort(unique(bindf$integrity_interval))
identity_bins <- sort(unique(bindf$identity_interval))
```

### 3.1 Recovery rate heatmaps (Fig 5B)

```{r, plot_heatmap_fun, echo=FALSE}
library(patchwork)
library(cowplot) # for get_legend

plot_recovery_heatmap <- function(scen){
  # Heatmap
  # mean number of simulated TEs per replicate, in white on dark cells and black on light cells
  n_labels <- heat_data |>
    filter(scenario == scen, n_reps > 0) |>
    mutate(label = case_when(n_mean >= 1000 ~ sprintf("%.1fk", n_mean / 1000),
                             n_mean >= 1 ~ sprintf("%.0f", n_mean),
                             TRUE ~ "<1"),
           label_colour = ifelse(rate < 0.6, "white", "black"))

  heat_p <- ggplot(heat_data |> filter(scenario == scen), aes(x=integrity_interval, y=identity_interval, fill=rate)) +
    geom_tile(color="grey80") +
    geom_text(data = n_labels, aes(label = label, colour = label_colour), size = 1.8) +
    scale_colour_identity() +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option="cividis", na.value = "grey85", limits = c(0, 1)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = rel(1.2)),
            axis.text.x = element_text(size = rel(1.2), angle=45, hjust=1),
            axis.title.x = element_text(size = rel(1.2)),
            axis.title.y = element_text(size = rel(1.2)),
            legend.position="none",
            panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black")) +
    labs(x="Integrity bin", y="Identity bin", fill="Rate")

  # Top marginal barplot
  top_p <- ggplot(marg_x |> filter(scenario == scen), aes(x=integrity_interval, y=rate, fill=rate)) +
    geom_col() +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax), width = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = integrity_bins) +  # keep all bins so bars stay aligned with the heatmap
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option="cividis", guide="none", limits = c(0, 1)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25)) +
    labs(title = scen) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = rel(1.5)),
            axis.text.x=element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.x=element_blank(),
            axis.title.y = element_text(size = rel(1.5)),
            legend.position="none",
            panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black")) +
    labs(x=NULL, y="Pooled rate")

  # Right marginal barplot (flip coordinates)
  right_p <- ggplot(marg_y |> filter(scenario == scen), aes(x=identity_interval, y=rate, fill=rate)) +
    geom_col() +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax), width = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = identity_bins) +  # keep all bins so bars stay aligned with the heatmap
    coord_flip() +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option="cividis", guide="none", limits = c(0, 1)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
    theme(axis.text.y=element_blank(), axis.ticks.y=element_blank(),
            axis.title.x = element_text(size = rel(1.5)),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = rel(1.5), angle=45, hjust=1),
            legend.position="none",
            panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black")) +
    labs(x=NULL, y="Pooled rate")

  # Grab the legend from a dummy plot with the same fill scale
  legend_p <- ggplot(heat_data |> filter(scenario == scen), aes(x=integrity_interval,
                                    y=identity_interval, fill=rate)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option="cividis", limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(fill="Rate") +
    theme(legend.position="right")

  legend_g <- patchwork::wrap_elements(get_legend(legend_p))

  # assemble top row (top_p + empty)
  top_row <- top_p + plot_spacer() +
    plot_layout(widths = c(2,1))  # adjust widths top row

  # assemble main row (heatmap + right)
  main_row <- heat_p + right_p +
    plot_layout(widths = c(2,1))  # right_p half the width

  # combine vertically (top half height of heatmap)
  combined <- top_row / main_row +
    plot_layout(heights = c(1,2))  # top half height of heatmap

  # put legend on top-right using | operator
  combined | legend_g
}
```

### 3.4 Binomial GLMM: identity vs integrity dependence

Recovery rises steeply with identity (≈0 below 0.5, ≈0.95 above 0.75), while integrity only
matters in the lowest bin (< 0.1), where recovery plateaus at ≈0.70-0.77 even at identity 0.95.
The main model is built to follow that shape, per scenario:

`cbind(recovered, total - recovered) ~ ns(identity, df = 3) * integrity_low + (1 | rep) + (1 | obs)`

* `ns(identity, df = 3)`: natural cubic spline of the identity bin midpoint (allows the threshold).
  df is capped at (number of identity bins - 2) so the spline cannot pass through every point
  and oscillate between them; scenario 4 has only 4 identity bins and gets df = 2.
* `integrity_low`: integrity bin `[0.0-0.1)` vs the rest (`>=0.1`, the reference level).
* `(1 | obs)`: observation-level random effect per cell × replicate, absorbing the extra-binomial
  variation between cells (the dispersion ratio, Pearson χ² / residual df, should be ≤ 1).
* `rep_sd` near 0 (singular fit) means the replicates do not differ beyond sampling noise.

Likelihood-ratio tests (LRT) drop all terms involving one variable (main effect + interaction).
With ~180,000 TEs per replicate almost any term is significant, so compare the size of the LRT
statistics rather than p-values. The two linear models (identity and integrity as bin midpoints,
centred at 0.5 and scaled so one unit is one bin; odds ratios per 0.1 increase) are kept for
reference: they cannot follow the identity threshold or the low-integrity plateau, so their
integrity statistics understate the effect of the lowest integrity bin.

```{r, glmm_recovery, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(lme4)
library(splines)

bin_mid_c <- function(interval){
  (as.numeric(sub('^\\[([0-9.]+)-.*', '\\1', interval)) + 0.05 - 0.5) * 10
}

glmm_df <- bindf %>%
  filter(total > 0) %>%
  mutate(identity = bin_mid_c(identity_interval),
         integrity = bin_mid_c(integrity_interval),
         integrity_low = factor(ifelse(integrity_interval == '[0.0-0.1)', '<0.1', '>=0.1'), levels = c('>=0.1', '<0.1')),
         rep = factor(rep),
         obs = factor(row_number()))

# identity / integrity terms and random effects of each model; the first is the main model
# (%d = spline df, set per scenario in fit_recovery_glmm)
glmm_specs <- list(
  list(identity = "ns(identity, df = %d)", integrity = "integrity_low", re = "(1 | rep) + (1 | obs)"),
  list(identity = "identity", integrity = "integrity", re = "(1 | rep) + (1 | obs)"),
  list(identity = "identity", integrity = "integrity", re = "(1 | rep)")
)

fit_recovery_glmm <- function(scen, spec){
  df <- glmm_df |> filter(scenario == scen)
  fit <- function(fixed) glmer(as.formula(paste("cbind(recovered, total - recovered) ~", fixed, "+", spec$re)),
                               data = df, family = binomial, control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5)))
  identity_term <- if (grepl("%d", spec$identity)) sprintf(spec$identity, min(3, n_distinct(df$identity) - 2)) else spec$identity
  model <- paste(identity_term, "*", spec$integrity, "+", spec$re)
  full <- fit(paste(identity_term, "*", spec$integrity))
  lrt_identity <- anova(fit(spec$integrity), full)
  lrt_integrity <- anova(fit(identity_term), full)
  fe <- coef(summary(full))
  list(
    model_fit = full,
    fixed = data.frame(scenario = scen, model = model, term = rownames(fe), estimate = fe[, "Estimate"], se = fe[, "Std. Error"],
                       odds_ratio = exp(fe[, "Estimate"]), z = fe[, "z value"], p = fe[, "Pr(>|z|)"], row.names = NULL),
    lrt = data.frame(scenario = scen, model = model,
                     n_cells = nrow(df),
                     rep_sd = attr(VarCorr(full)$rep, "stddev"),
                     singular = isSingular(full),
                     dispersion = sum(residuals(full, type = "pearson")^2) / df.residual(full),
                     identity_chisq = lrt_identity$Chisq[2], identity_df = lrt_identity$Df[2], identity_p = lrt_identity$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2],
                     integrity_chisq = lrt_integrity$Chisq[2], integrity_df = lrt_integrity$Df[2], integrity_p = lrt_integrity$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2], row.names = NULL)
  )
}

glmm_fits <- unlist(lapply(glmm_specs, function(spec) lapply(scenarios, fit_recovery_glmm, spec = spec)), recursive = FALSE)
glmm_fixed <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(glmm_fits, `[[`, "fixed"))
glmm_lrt <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(glmm_fits, `[[`, "lrt"))
glmm_main <- setNames(lapply(glmm_fits[seq_along(scenarios)], `[[`, "model_fit"), scenarios)

kable(glmm_lrt, digits = 4, caption = "LRT for identity terms and integrity terms (each dropping main effect + interaction)")
kable(glmm_fixed, digits = 4, caption = "Fixed effects of the full models (linear models: odds ratio per 0.1 increase)")
write.table(glmm_lrt, file = paste0(OUT, "sim_tair10_sd_scenarioAll_recovery_glmm_lrt.tsv"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
write.table(glmm_fixed, file = paste0(OUT, "sim_tair10_sd_scenarioAll_recovery_glmm_fixed.tsv"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
```

**A**: LRT χ² of the main model for dropping the identity terms vs the integrity terms.
**B**: recovery rate against identity. Large points with error bars are pooled rates,
sum(recovered) / sum(total), for integrity < 0.1 and ≥ 0.1 (mean ± SD of the 5 replicates);
small light points are the 9 individual integrity bins ≥ 0.1 (mean of replicate rates), showing
that they behave alike. Lines are the main GLMM's fixed-effect predictions (random effects at 0,
i.e. a typical cell).

```{r, plot_glmm, echo=FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.asp = 0.65, out.width="90%"}
plotwidth <- 10
plotheight <- 6.5
integrity_cols <- c('<0.1' = '#D55E00', '>=0.1' = '#0072B2')

# A: dumbbell of LRT chi-square, main model
lrt_long <- glmm_lrt %>%
  filter(grepl("^ns\\(", model)) %>%
  select(scenario, identity_chisq, integrity_chisq) %>%
  pivot_longer(-scenario, names_to = "terms", values_to = "chisq") %>%
  mutate(terms = sub("_chisq", "", terms))

glmm_lrt_p <- ggplot(lrt_long, aes(x = chisq, y = scenario)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = scenario), colour = "grey70", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = terms), size = 3) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(identity = '#0072B2', integrity = '#D55E00')) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black")) +
  labs(x = "LRT chi-square (log scale)", y = NULL, colour = "Terms dropped", title = "A")

# B: observed pooled rates and model predictions against identity
obs_grouped <- glmm_df %>%
  group_by(scenario, rep, integrity_low, identity_interval, identity) %>%
  summarise(rate = sum(recovered) / sum(total), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(scenario, integrity_low, identity_interval, identity) %>%
  summarise(sd = sd(rate), rate = mean(rate), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(identity_mid = identity / 10 + 0.5)

obs_bins <- heat_data %>%
  filter(n_reps > 0, integrity_interval != '[0.0-0.1)') %>%
  mutate(identity_mid = bin_mid_c(identity_interval) / 10 + 0.5)

# predictions only over the identity range observed for each integrity group (no extrapolation)
glmm_pred <- glmm_df %>%
  group_by(scenario, integrity_low) %>%
  summarise(id_min = min(identity), id_max = max(identity), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(scenario, integrity_low) %>%
  reframe(identity = seq(id_min, id_max, length.out = 100)) %>%
  group_by(scenario) %>%
  group_modify(function(nd, key) mutate(nd, rate = predict(glmm_main[[key$scenario]], newdata = nd, re.form = NA, type = "response"))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(identity_mid = identity / 10 + 0.5)

glmm_fit_p <- ggplot(obs_grouped, aes(x = identity_mid, y = rate, colour = integrity_low)) +
  geom_point(data = obs_bins, aes(x = identity_mid, y = rate), inherit.aes = FALSE,
             colour = '#0072B2', alpha = 0.25, size = 1, position = position_jitter(width = 0.01, height = 0, seed = 1)) +
  geom_line(data = glmm_pred, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = pmax(rate - sd, 0), ymax = pmin(rate + sd, 1)), width = 0.02) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~scenario, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = integrity_cols) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black")) +
  labs(x = "Identity (bin midpoint)", y = "Recovery rate", colour = "Integrity", title = "B")

glmm_p <- glmm_lrt_p / glmm_fit_p + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1.4))
glmm_p
```
